note: Track beat, step 7: the metronome heard as beats 2 and 4. Count against a slow click, clap in the gaps, then clap eighths over it; the faster tempos are moves, not a stage choice, so the text names no selector. Missing: a metronome that sounds only beats 2 and 4 of a set tempo and shows the bar; the block uses a plain click at half the tempo and the count is the player's own.

exercise.title: The metronome on 2 and 4
exercise.why: When the click sounds only on beats 2 and 4, nothing gives you beats 1 and 3, so your own count has to carry the bar from one click to the next.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome: a slow click. Count four beats to every two clicks, so that you say "two" and "four" on the clicks and "one" and "three" in the gaps. Then clap on all four beats as you count.
Practice until every second clap lands right on a click.

Press Play below to start the metronome again. Keep counting, and clap only on "one" and "three", in the gaps between the clicks.
If the click starts to sound like beat 1, stop clapping, count "two" and "four" on the clicks again, and come back in.

Press Play below to start the metronome again. Clap eighths, two claps to a beat, so that four claps fit from one click to the next, and keep counting.
Practice until the click still lands on your "two" and "four" after many bars.
